decision.title: Persist recovery tokens in SQLite
decision.chosen: Use the existing SQLite database for recovery tokens.

source.spec_rationale: One local service must retain token state across restart; the existing database avoids a second persistence service.
source.implementation_evidence: The committed implementation writes a token row before acknowledging creation. A restart test passes. No multi-host deployment or throughput test was performed.

cases.reference:
## Context

The local recovery service needs token state to survive a restart and already uses SQLite.

## Decision

Use the existing SQLite database for recovery tokens so acknowledgements follow persisted rows.

## Consequences

Later recovery work must use the token rows. Restart behaviour is verified; multi-host operation and throughput remain unverified.

Self-review: The consequences match the supplied implementation evidence; no unverified behaviour is claimed.

confidence: high

decision.title: Deduplicate webhook jobs
decision.chosen: Use a unique delivery key in the existing job table.

source.spec_rationale: The provider may deliver the same event twice. The service already has a job table with a unique-key constraint.
source.implementation_evidence: The same delivery key is inserted once and the second enqueue is acknowledged without a second job. A duplicate-event test passes. Different event ordering was not changed.

cases.reference:
## Situation

Webhook deliveries may repeat; the existing job table supports a unique key.

## Decision

Use a unique delivery key in the existing job table to prevent duplicate jobs.

## Trade-offs

Delivery-key storage is retained; different-event ordering remains unchanged.

## Follow-up

Keep the duplicate-event regression test. Do not infer ordering guarantees from deduplication.

Self-review: The consequences match the supplied implementation evidence; no unverified behaviour is claimed.

decision.title: Use a durable retry ledger
decision.chosen: Keep retry attempts in the existing durable database.

source.spec_rationale: The accepted transient retry record in ADR-0041 loses attempt history after restart. This settled choice preserves that history.
source.implementation_evidence: The retry count and next-attempt time survive the tested restart. No ADR status or supersession metadata has been changed; the caller owns recording it.

cases.reference:
## Context

ADR-0041, Use transient retry records, stores attempt history transiently and loses it after restart.

## Decision

Keep retry attempts in the existing durable database so attempt history survives restart.

## Consequences

The retry count and next-attempt time survive the tested restart. The caller must record any supersession metadata; this body does not change ADR-0041 status.

Self-review: The consequences match the supplied implementation evidence; no unverified behaviour is claimed.

source.spec_rationale: The deployment has one host and a durable data volume. Remote replication is excluded from this release.

cases.reference:

One host has an existing durable data volume; remote replication is outside this release.

## Decision

Store attachment blobs in the existing local data directory.

## Consequences

The local write/read test passes. Disk-loss recovery and backup restore remain unverified; later work must not assume replication.

Self-review: The consequences match the supplied implementation evidence; no unverified behaviour is claimed.
